source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
DC Blox's Birmingham facility publishes 5 MW of IT capacity across 294,000 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation baseline, 5 MW supports roughly 500 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same power envelope supports roughly 125 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so which figure applies to any given deployment is not known from this source.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications, so no reading of qualification for specific workload tiers is possible from this data. The operator name field is blank in the structured source, meaning the operator has not been confirmed through the spec page as read. Tenant information is not published.

Among the 11 data center facilities mapped in Alabama, this is the only one for which this site has read a published megawatt figure, making DC Blox Birmingham ranked first in the state by published IT capacity, and accounting for all 5 MW of the state total on record here. That ranking reflects the absence of published figures from other Alabama facilities rather than a confirmed lead over them. Alabama is a minor data center market by any measure derivable from this dataset, and 5 MW is a modest footprint relative to major AI infrastructure campuses elsewhere in the country.
